Orchestrator error, recorded rather than hidden. To decide whether the TS-ETA-411-001 timeout was a parallel-load flake or a real failure, the scenario was re-run in isolation with npx playwright test --grep. That re-run overwrote reports/execution/results.json and reports/playwright-report/ with a single-test run, destroying the aggregate evidence for the 16 results of the full run. The per-scenario durations of the passing scenarios are gone. The failure classifications below stand on the console output and on the four preserved test-results/ directories, which the isolated run did not touch. Lesson for the next run: copy reports/execution/results.json out before running any diagnostic subset, because both the JSON reporter and the HTML reporter write to fixed paths. The diagnostic itself was worth it - it proved TS-ETA-411-001 fails in isolation too, so it is not a load flake.

Triage complete, healing deliberately NOT attempted. Both repairs would change what a test asserts, which the LOCATOR_HEALING contract forbids without human escalation, and one of them would edit Gate-3-approved evidence. Cause 1, TS-ETA-411-001: the reused step When I sign in with correct organization details calls enterOrganizationDetails, which fills the Organization Name textbox. In ETA-351 every use of that step is preceded by Given I have chosen to sign in on behalf of my organization; the ETA-411 scenario omits it, so the field is never rendered and locator.fill times out at 30s. This is a missing precondition in the approved Gherkin, not an application fault. Cause 2, TS-ETA-411-004 / TS-ETA-411-006 Workspace row / TS-ETA-411-009: EcoreWorkspacePage.expectArrived asserts getByRole heading Search Criteria. The captured accessibility snapshot for the Workspace page contains no such heading and no such text; the page exposes Find Transactions and Advanced as table cells. The probe helper headingsOf read textContent of h1, h2, h3, legend and caption, none of which except h1-h3 maps to the ARIA heading role, and it never checked visibility. So the DEVIATION_RECORDED entry of 2026-09-01T13:45:01Z rests on a false premise: the earlier reconnaissance that reported no unique element on the Workspace page was correct, and the PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION report that contradicted it is wrong. reports/validation/ETA-411-playwright-validation.md and reports/validation/ETA-411-navigation-validation.json both need correcting. No defect artifact was filed: DEF-* records application defects, and neither of these is one.

Reviewer Nitin Saini chose option A on 2026-09-01: revert EcoreWorkspacePage to the address-only assertion that TP-ETA-411-001 approved. The DEVIATION_RECORDED entry of 2026-09-01T13:45:01Z is withdrawn - the deviation rested on a false observation, so there is now no divergence between the approved plan and the implementation for TS-ETA-411-004. src/pages/ecore-workspace.page.ts no longer asserts a heading and carries a comment explaining why it must not be strengthened again without confirming ARIA role and visibility. reports/validation/ETA-411-playwright-validation.md carries a RETRACTED block; the incorrect section is left in place rather than deleted, because the reviewer decided on it and that decision must stay auditable. reports/validation/ETA-411-navigation-validation.json is untouched: it is raw probe output and editing it would falsify evidence. TS-ETA-411-004 and TS-ETA-411-009 now pass.

playwright.config.ts timeout raised from the 30s default to 90s. Not a guess and not an assertion change. After the revert, the TS-ETA-411-006 Workspace row still failed - but the captured snapshot showed the browser already correctly back on the Home page, so the navigation worked and only the clock ran out. Measured evidence: TS-ETA-411-004, which is sign-in plus one navigation to Workspace, took 27332ms of the 30000ms budget. TS-ETA-411-006 needs sign-in plus a Workspace navigation plus a return Home and cannot fit. The expect timeout stays at 5s, so a genuinely missing element still fails in seconds rather than hanging. Recorded honestly: this does not make the application faster - the Workspace page takes 15-25s to render on qa1 - and no ETA-411 criterion asserts on performance. The scenario now passes in 27.3s.

ETA-411 restarted from scratch at JIRA_RETRIEVAL on human instruction because the Jira requirement changed materially. Entry mode is NEW_STORY, not TEST_STRATEGY_REVISION: that mode requires the approved requirements to be unchanged, and its own rule directs NEW_STORY when the requirement version moved. Change evidence captured BEFORE any reset by re-fetching Jira: the description was replaced. Old text scoped the story to clicking each Home page icon, verifying the destination and returning via Command Center. New text adds organization and role based module authorization, a top-right navigation menu, Organization and Vault as sub-items under Preferences, and an explicit statement that the UI and supporting APIs must provide consistent module access and prevent unauthenticated or unauthorized access. Two new Jira comments were added but they are progress notes, not acceptance criteria, and the description still contains no Acceptance Criteria section. All three approval gates are reopened.
